brief: The sill under the canvas has said "Day 12 · Afternoon" since before the loop and has never named the season — while nine systems now read season(). A viewer who loads the page in deep winter has no way to know it is winter unless they already know what this town looks like in July. Say where in the year we are, in the frame, in the diorama own register: #plate is serif and #ticker is italic serif, so this is a museum label and not a HUD. Keep #daytime tabular clock. Why now: it is the cheapest possible fix to the largest gap in the piece, and b27 needs a viewer who can already read the year before it gives them a way to travel through it.
successLooksLike: Someone loading the page at any instant can name the season within about three seconds, without waiting for anything to change, and can still read the day and the hour as before.
avoid: Do not add a second row to the sill — it is one baseline-aligned flex row, and #ticker and #stats are already display:none under 640px. Do not draw text on the canvas. Do not touch SEASON_START or the anchor.
